en.name: Delirium Detection Score (DDS)
en.shortDescription: Bedside ICU assessment tool to monitor and quantify delirium severity through eight clinical criteria
en.longDescription: ## Definition & Clinical Context The DDS (Delirium Detection Score) is a bedside assessment tool designed to monitor and quantify delirium severity in ICU patients. It was originally developed and validated in surgical ICU patients [1]. The instrument comprises eight clinical criteria: - orientation - hallucinations - agitation - anxiety - seizures - tremor - paroxysmal sweating - altered sleep-wake rhythm The DDS score increases with delirium severity. ## Included Concepts This concept set contains a single custom concept, as no equivalent exists in standard terminologies (SNOMED, LOINC). ## References [1] Otter H, Martin J, Bäsell K, et al. Validity and reliability of the DDS for severity of delirium in the ICU. *Neurocrit Care*. 2005;2(2):150-154. doi:10.1385/NCC:2:2:150. PMID: 16159057

fr.name: Delirium Detection Score (DDS)
fr.shortDescription: Outil d'évaluation au lit du patient en réanimation, mesurant la sévérité du delirium à partir de huit critères cliniques
fr.longDescription: ## Définition et contexte clinique Le DDS (Delirium Detection Score) est un outil d'évaluation au lit du patient conçu pour surveiller et quantifier la sévérité du délirium chez les patients de réanimation. Il a été initialement développé et validé chez des patients de réanimation chirurgicale [1]. L'instrument comprend huit critères cliniques : - orientation - hallucinations - agitation - anxiété - convulsions - tremblements - sudation paroxystique - altération du rythme veille-sommeil Le score DDS augmente avec la sévérité du délirium. ## Concepts inclus Ce concept set contient un seul concept custom, aucun équivalent n'existant dans les terminologies standard (SNOMED, LOINC). ## Références [1] Otter H, Martin J, Bäsell K, et al. Validity and reliability of the DDS for severity of delirium in the ICU. *Neurocrit Care*. 2005;2(2):150-154. doi:10.1385/NCC:2:2:150. PMID: 16159057

reviews.comments:
## Summary
**Approved.** Used in QI07 (pain/sedation/delirium assessment). No standard OMOP concept exists for DDS; the INDICATE custom concept (>= 2,100,000,000, [issue #3](https://github.com/indicate-eu/data-dictionary/issues/3)) is acceptable as a transitional solution.

## Use in our quality indicators
- Used in QI07 (Pain, sedation, delirium).
- CQL: all 1 concept(s) of the set are referenced in [`IndicateQi07PainSedationDelir.cql`](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQi07PainSedationDelir.cql?plain=1) ([2100000002](https://github.com/umg-minai/cql-indicate-qi/blob/d63eb84a308d5586fcede0b7e3fa73abf6b6761c/cql/IndicateQi07PainSedationDelir.cql?plain=1#L47); each ID links to its code definition).
